A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TrendFact and FactISR, retaining the same core dataset, method components and many results. The main text, equations, figures, tables and all appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial expansion and retitling.

before.justification: v2 Tables 2–3 report original fact-verification, explanation-generation and component-evaluation results on TrendFact.

after.justification: v3 Tables 2–6 report original retrieval, verification, explanation, ablation and efficiency results. Tables 10–11 also retain earlier gold-evidence results.

M1.justification: v2 FactISR combines evidence triangulation and rewarded self-reflection. v3 adds Dynamic Evidence Augmentation, which inserts additional retrieved evidence during reasoning when the model emits an evidence-request signal (Section 4.2; Figures 9–10). This changes the inference procedure; the existing triangulation workflow and reward-decoding equation are substantially retained.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the 7,643 Chinese claims from trending platforms and CHEF. v3 adds an evaluated retrieval task over a 66,217-entry evidence library with publication dates, plus verification and explanation under retrieved-evidence conditions. This substantially expands task coverage and the evidence conditions encountered during evaluation.

E2.justification: v3 adds QwQ-32B and Qwen3-32B thinking/non-thinking comparisons, alongside BM25 with/without dates, text-embedding-ada-002 and bge-m3 retrieval comparisons. PROGRAM-FC and CLAIMDECOMP remain. The explicit QwQ-Preview CoT comparator disappears, while o1-preview remains in the gold-evidence appendix rather than the new main comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 introduces retrieval R@1/2/3/5 and HCPI evaluation, retrieved-evidence experiments, and FactISR evaluations on two newer backbones. Appendix J changes the stated RLM output limit from v2's 300 to 5k, retaining 300 for LLMs, and specifies 3k retrieval truncation. Its three-addition DEA limit conflicts with the two-addition limit in Figure 9.

E4.justification: v2 incrementally adds ET and ISR on QwQ-Preview. v3 replaces this with separate removal of DEA, ET and ISR on two backbones (Table 5), adds DEA generation-time/input-evidence-length analysis (Table 6), and presents a new DEA case (Figure 10). The original cold-wave reflection example is retained as translated Figure 11.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty analyses. Both present point estimates; the additional results do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds retrieval, HCPI, retrieved-evidence and efficiency results. For example, bge-m3 achieves R@5 of 78.97, and FactISR improves retrieved-evidence QwQ-32B accuracy from 72.67 to 74.32. Every retained standalone gold-evidence baseline score matches v2 exactly in Tables 10–11; the earlier CoT/ET/ET+ISR rows are removed. The new main scores are not same-setting changes from v2.

T1.justification: Appendix F adds formal influence and HCPI definitions (Equations 2–3), combining risk-weighted logarithmic hotspot indicators, ECS and asymmetric label-error penalties. This introduces a substantive new mathematical evaluation framework, although some predicted-label cases are unspecified. The reward-decoding equation and five-level ECS definition remain unchanged; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion redefine TrendFact's central contribution around hotspot perception across retrieval, verification and explanation, extending the earlier emphasis on Chinese explanations. HCPI and the dated evidence library become central contributions, and FactISR becomes a three-component method. The broad claims that existing models struggle and FactISR helps remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds interpretations attributing higher HCPI to RLM reasoning about hotspot attributes and DEA efficiency to reduced noisy evidence and redundant reasoning. These extend the existing discussion without replacing its explanation of concise RLM outputs and lower lexical scores. The labor-cost limitations in Section 7 remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands documentation with staged filtering prompts, claim-rewriting factors, annotation-review criteria, evidence-library construction instructions, and HCPI weights, imputation and scaling. Hardware changes from four to two A100 GPUs. Some earlier specifics disappear, including GPT-3.5 implementation details for traditional baselines and the three-independent-reviewer count. The code/data access statement remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 substantially repositions TrendFact against prior benchmarks around missing hotspot assessment and comprehensive task coverage (Section 2; Table 1), extending the earlier Chinese-explanation gap. It adds BGE-M3, DeepSeek-V3 and Qwen3 references while removing several Wikipedia, table and dialogue verification references.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the abstract, motivation, contributions, construction narrative and results discussion. The former Baselines section becomes a dedicated FactISR section, comparator descriptions move into experimental setup, and the appendices are extensively reorganized. The title, author order and contact information also change.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are redesigned to include hotspot attributes, evidence-library construction and DEA. Table 1 gains hotspot and task columns, and new retrieval, ablation and efficiency tables restructure the results presentation. Earlier gold-evidence results and ECS definitions move to appendices; new workflow displays appear, and the reflection example is translated and reformatted.

improvement.justification: v3 addresses an important evaluation gap by testing evidence retrieval and verification with retrieved evidence, while retaining the standalone gold-evidence results. Detailed construction workflows and two-backbone ablations substantially strengthen auditability and support for the method's components. These gains outweigh the loss of CoT/gold-evidence FactISR comparisons, although the inconsistent DEA limit and incomplete HCPI prediction cases remain material specification weaknesses.
